articles.title: Taylor Frankie Paul Confirms She Got Engaged on Pulled ‘Bachelorette’ Season, Reveals What Happened After Filming
articles.excerpt: The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star opens up about what unfolded after The Bachelorette including reconnecting with ex Dakota Mortensen.
articles.content:
The 'Secret Lives of Mormon Wives' star opens up about what unfolded after she returned home to Utah, including reconnecting with ex Dakota Mortensen.

Taylor Frankie Paul is revealing major details surrounding her Bachelorette season that viewers will likely never get to see — including that she got engaged and what went wrong.

During Thursday’s episode of Hulu’s Get Real podcast, an exclusive clip from the upcoming fifth season of The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives shows Paul spilling what happened to fellow castmembers Jessi Draper, Mikayla Matthews and Mayci Neeley.

The clip begins with the women asking Paul if she was intimate with anyone in the Bachelor Nation franchise’s infamous fantasy suites. Paul seemingly shakes her head no.

Without naming him, Draper points out that Paul’s reported final pick on the season, Doug Mason, shares some similarities with Paul’s ex-boyfriend and the father of one of her son’s, Dakota Mortensen, including their initials and the fact that they’re both from Idaho.

“They have the same initials. They’re both from Idaho,” Draper says. “It’s so weird.”

“I didn’t learn all that until later,” Paul responds.

Paul then reveals that she received an unexpected proposal — and said yes.

“He did get down on one knee and proposed,” Paul says. “I was shocked.”

Draper replies, “He told us he wasn’t going to,” referring to when she and other Mormon Wives castmembers visited Paul while she was filming The Bachelorette.

Paul says she believed the same and confirms that she accepted the proposal. However, she adds, “Then, I came home.”

After returning to Utah, Paul says she began texting Mortensen again.

“I don’t know how it led to it, but he came over,” she says, seemingly implying that the two hooked up — something that has been widely speculated.

Paul, who founded the Mormon influencer group known as MomTok, was set to make her debut as the Bachelorette on March 22. However, ABC pulled the season just three days before its scheduled premiere after TMZ published video footage showing the events that led to Paul’s 2023 arrest following an argument with Mortensen.

Paul pleaded guilty to aggravated assault in 2023 as part of a plea agreement that resulted in her other charges being dismissed. Her plea was held in abeyance, with the felony charge set to be reduced to a misdemeanor if she completed the terms of the agreement. The incident was later chronicled on The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives.

Two days before ABC pulled the season, Paul spoke with The Hollywood Reporter at a press event in New York City, where she addressed widespread TikTok speculation that Mason was her final pick.

“I’ve seen a lot of spoilers. However, none of them have been really correct,” she said at the time. “So for me, I’m just like, I guess keep putting out those incorrect spoilers. For the audience, I would want to watch to see if they’re actually true, because there have been so many different ones. How do you even know which one is even it at this point?”

In the weeks following the cancellation, Utah authorities investigated additional domestic violence allegations involving Paul and Mortensen. Mortensen reported an alleged 2024 incident to West Jordan police in February, while Draper police separately investigated another incident involving the former couple. In April, the Salt Lake County District Attorney’s Office announced that it would not file new charges against Paul after reviewing the cases.

Production on The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives season five was also halted in March amid the fallout. The season will now premiere on Hulu on Sept. 10.

In July, before the season five premiere date was announced, Mormon Wives co-star Miranda Hope told THR that she hadn’t been in touch with Paul.

“We haven’t really spoken recently,” she said. “But I genuinely hope that she’s doing well, and from what I know and what I hear, it seems like and sounds like she’s doing better. I truly wish nothing but the best for her.”

Nick Minicucci was one of the most productive quarterbacks in the country last year.

That has earned the Delaware starter a heap of preseason recognition, including Conference USA preseason Offensive Player of the Year and watch list status for various awards.

While appreciating the notice and the notoriety, Minicucci’s sentiments are centered on his team, not himself.

As the Blue Hens kick off the 2026 season Sept. 3 against Merrimack at 7 p.m. at Delaware Stadium, Minicucci welcomes the opportunity to begin creating new successes while expanding his repertoire.

“I don't accept any of those because it's preseason,” Minicucci said of the early hype. “Why do I care about something I haven't earned yet? That stuff's all just out there. It's outside noise to me, and I don't really care about it. It feels good, but what is that going to do for me on Thursday?”

The fourth-year Blue Hen will be focused on operating coach Ryan Carty’s spread offense at peak efficiency while becoming more comfortable with his surrounding playmakers, which include several transfer arrivals.

“I really want to win a conference championship,” Minicucci added. “I don't really care about personal accolades. I've never really been that way. I'm not a selfish guy. I really care about just the team, and I want us to win and win together. A Conference USA championship here at Delaware would mean the world to me.”

Minicucci was one of just two quarterbacks last year nationally to have at least 3,500 passing yards and 10 rushing TDs, along with Vanderbilt’s Heisman runner-up Diego Pavia.

Carty has been pleased with Minicucci’s ongoing quest to be better, despite his 2025 accomplishments. Being a second-year starter allows him to have a deeper grasp of how to best move the football, and try new, different and potentially better things.

“Nick's done a really nice job,” Carty said on the eve of his fifth season as coach. “He's always asking for more. There's never a day that goes by that he's going to rest and say ‘I made it. I’m good.’ It's always something that's driving him.”

Carty has never lost a home opener during his coaching career, including his time on the staffs at New Hampshire (2007-17) and Sam Houston (2018-21) . . . Delaware is 23-4 in home games under Carty . . . Delaware threw more passes last year (540) than any other FBS team except Florida Atlantic (582).

articles.title: Enes Kanter Freedom files lawsuit against Sky following ejection, ban after altercation with Natasha Cloud
articles.excerpt: Enes Kanter Freedom has filed a lawsuit against the Chicago Sky, claiming his First Amendment rights were violated following his ejection and ban from Wintrust Arena.
articles.content:
The lawsuit stated Freedom was 'peacefully exercising my First Amendment rights' before ejection

Enes Kanter Freedom mulls lawsuit against Chicago Sky, responds to team owner's remarks

Enes Kanter Freedom talks to OutKick about the Chicago Sky's ejection and ban as well as a potential lawsuit against the team.

Enes Kanter Freedom is taking legal action against the Chicago Sky following his ejection from Wintrust Arena following an altercation with guard Natasha Cloud during a game against the Indiana Fever. 

Freedom filed his federal complaint in U.S. District Court, where he said he was "peacefully exercising my First Amendment rights" by sitting near the baseline and wearing a T-shirt that read, "WOMAN noun, adult human female." Freedom was banned indefinitely from Wintrust Arena by the Sky, and he said he may be pursuing legal action because of it. 

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Turkish-American former basketball player and human rights activist Enes Kanter Freedom is seen prior to a game between the Indiana Fever and the Chicago Sky at Wintrust Arena in Chicago, Ill., on Aug. 23, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

Freedom’s lawsuit names Chicago Women’s Basketball Operations, LLC, which operates the Sky, the Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority (MPEA), which financed and built Wintrust Arena as a public project, and the City of Chicago as defendants, claiming they "combined and conspired, and acted jointly to execute their conspiracy, to discriminate against Plaintiff based on Plaintiff’s verbal and demonstrable expression of viewpoint and gender identity when they wrongfully ejected Plaintiff from a recent WNBA game."

"Defendants compounded and exacerbated Plaintiff’s injuries when they subsequently banned Plaintiff indefinitely from attendance," the lawsuit obtained by OutKick read. 

The lawsuit adds that Freedom "believes deeply and advocates forcefully that the integrity of women-only sports must be protected, and he has been explicit in many public appearances on this point." 

The suit also reiterates a point Freedom has made on numerous occasions, that he self-identifies as a player who is eligible to participate in the WNBA "because such declaration is all that is required by WNBA’s rules." Freedom has received backlash for his stance, which was also mentioned in the lawsuit. 

"Plaintiff has been the target of a torrent of hateful attacks and discriminatory actions based on Plaintiff’s viewpoint and gender identity," the lawsuit read. 

CHICAGO SKY OWNER OPENS UP ON ENES KANTER FREEDOM EJECTION, MAKES ANALOGY TO SHOOTING A GUN

The lawsuit proceeds to break down the events on Aug. 23 in the eyes of Freedom, which began with his manager sending a "courteous text message" to Sky GM Jeff Pagliocca, his old personal trainer, to inform him the former NBA center would be attending the game. Pagliocca allegedly responded, "Appreciate the text," but Sky owner Michael Alter allegedly alerted Wintrust Arena Security of Freedom’s expected attendance. 

It continues by saying Freedom was harassed by Sky fans, many of whom used vulgar language including, "Get your b---- a—out of Chicago, f--- you b----, b---- a-- n-----!," among others. 

"None of these fans were warned or ejected, despite profanity and racial slurs being express violations of the WNBA Fan Code of Conduct," the lawsuit read. 

Former basketball player Enes Kanter Freedom and Natasha Cloud #9 of the Chicago Sky yell at one another during the second half between the Chicago Sky and the Indiana Fever at Wintrust Arena on August 23, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) (Michael Reaves/Getty Images)

During the third quarter of the game, Freedom stood and raised his arms in celebration of a three-pointer made by Sophie Cunningham, the Fever star who has also received vitriol for her stance on biological men participating in women’s sports. A few possessions later, Cloud made a shot, and following a timeout, she "initiated a vulgar, profanity-laced verbal tired directed at Plaintiff Freedom personally, and charged nearly half the length of the court toward where Plaintiff Freedom was sitting courtside," the lawsuit read. 

"Plaintiff Freedom believes that Cloud’s attack was motivated and triggered by the message on Plaintiff’s shirt and Plaintiff’s widely publicized viewpoint on protecting the integrity of women only sports," the lawsuit added. 

The lawsuit states that, while Freedom raised his arms "in confusion and disbelief," Cloud continued to scream out profanities in his direction "in violation of WNBA rules." Cloud was not ejected from the game, nor did the WNBA issue any disciplinary action. Alter also confirmed the Sky would not take action against Cloud. 

The lawsuit adds that Alter "subsequently mischaracterized the interaction" between Freedom and Cloud, claiming the former was "chirping" at her before the altercation. It also mentioned an interview Alter had with OutKick, where he likened what Freedom did to shooting a gun at someone. 

"I mean, to use an extreme example, when you shoot a gun at someone, you don’t get a warning, ‘Don’t do that again.’ Your action doesn’t deserve a warning. You take action that becomes a threat, you don’t get a warning," Alter told OutKick. 

Freedom claimed that damages against him continue "as long as the unconstitutional ban" from Wintrust Arena stays in effect. 

Former basketball player Enes Kanter Freedom looks on courtside during the first half between the Chicago Sky and the Indiana Fever at Wintrust Arena in Chicago on Aug. 23, 2026. (Getty Images)

Freedom requested the court declare the defendants violated his First Amendment rights by ejecting him from Wintrust Arena and indefinitely barring him from re-entry as well as"an award of nominal and compensatory damages for Plaintiff’s losses incurred."

"My T-shirt did what the whole [WNBA] apparently couldn’t: define a woman," Kanter’s X post with his lawsuit read. "No threats. No violence. Just biology. And somehow, that required a security escort. You don’t have to agree with my speech but you don’t get to silence me for it. I will not be intimidated. I will not be silenced. I will continue to stand for women and defend free speech." 

The Sky and MPEA did not immediately respond to a request for comment by OutKick regarding Kanter’s lawsuit. The City of Chicago doesn't comment on pending litigation, an official said.

Scott Thompson is a sports writer for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Foldable iPhone Ultra will have an average cost of $2,550, report says
articles.excerpt: Just how much will the foldable iPhone Ultra cost? A new report projects an average price of more than $2,500.
articles.content:
Just how much will the foldable iPhone Ultra cost? That's the biggest lingering question ahead of Apple's big iPhone launch event on Sept. 9.

Leaks point to a price of $2,000 or more, and now, a new report from the analysts at the market intelligence firm International Data Corporation (IDC) projects an average selling price of $2,550. The IDC has a solid reputation and is well known for its mobile market research in particular.

The foldable iPhone Ultra is a brand new product category for Apple, so there's no baseline to say how much it could cost. However, the latest IDC report backs reports that the iPhone Ultra will launch at above $2,000.

We should note that the iPhone Ultra won't necessarily set you back $2,550. The average selling price could be quite a bit higher than the starting price, as many consumers will pay more for configurations with more storage. Despite the high price, the IDC projects that Apple will sell more than 17 million iPhone Ultras by the end of 2027 and bring in more than $45.7 billion from the foldable.

"Apple’s entry into the foldable market has done more than reignite growth in a category that was losing momentum," said Nabila Popal, Senior Research Director of IDC Worldwide Quarterly Mobile Phone Tracker in a statement. "It has fundamentally altered the market’s trajectory. Without Apple, foldable shipments would have declined at a double-digit rate year over year." 

The $2,550 estimate gives us a clearer idea of what to expect from the iPhone Ultra. Some Apple analysts have projected a $2,399 launch price for the iPhone Ultra, and it could cost up to $3,000 with more storage.

IDC projects that Apple will capture around 40 percent of the global foldable market and account for more than half of the total value of foldables.

According to the IDC, the iPhone Ultra is expected to be such a hit that it will propel the foldable market forward as the only mobile category that experiences growth in 2026. The firm expects the rest of the global smartphone market to decline this year due to higher prices driven by ongoing global memory shortages.

"Perhaps most notably, Apple is positioned to challenge Huawei and Samsung for leadership in markets where they have long dominated, an extraordinary outcome for a product expected to be less than two years into its lifecycle," Popal said.

VANCOUVER, British Columbia--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- lululemon athletica inc. (NASDAQ:LULU) today announced financial results for the second quarter of fiscal 2026, which ended on August 2, 2026.

Meghan Frank, Interim Co-CEO and Chief Financial Officer, stated: "While we continue to navigate some challenging dynamics, we are taking a prudent approach with our revised full-year outlook. Our teams remain focused on accelerating growth by strengthening our product offerings, increasing our marketing investments, and maintaining disciplined expense management. Looking ahead, we have confidence in the strength of the lululemon brand, the deep connection we have with our guests and ambassadors, and the significant opportunities we see to drive long-term growth."

André Maestrini, Interim Co-CEO, President, and Chief Commercial Officer, stated: "We remain confident in our ability to take the right steps to strengthen our performance and deliver sustainable growth over time. I would like to thank our teams around the world for their focused efforts and continued commitment to lululemon. We look forward to welcoming our incoming CEO, Heidi O'Neill, next week as we begin an exciting new chapter for the company."

For the second quarter of 2026, compared to the second quarter of 2025:

  • Net revenue decreased 4% to $2.4 billion, or decreased 5% on a constant dollar basis.
    • Americas net revenue decreased 8%.
    • International net revenue increased 4%, or 2% on a constant dollar basis.
  • Comparable sales decreased 9%, or 10% on a constant dollar basis.
    • Americas comparable sales decreased 12%.
    • International comparable sales decreased 3%, or 6% on a constant dollar basis.
  • Gross profit decreased 1% to $1.5 billion and gross margin increased 200 basis points to 60.5%.
    • This includes $134.5 million of tariff refunds(1) which increased gross margin by 560 basis points.
  • Income from operations decreased 13% to $453.7 million and operating margin decreased 190 basis points to 18.8%.
    • The tariff refunds(1) of $134.5 million increased operating margin by 560 basis points.
  • The effective income tax rate for the second quarter of 2026 was 29.6%, compared to 30.5% for the second quarter of 2025.
  • Diluted earnings per share were $2.92 compared to $3.10 in the second quarter of 2025.
    • This includes $0.86 per share related to tariff refunds and associated interest(1), net of tax.
  • The Company repurchased 2.7 million of its shares for a cost of $330.0 million.
  • The Company opened nine net new company-operated stores during the second quarter, ending with 825 stores.
  • Americas net revenue decreased 8%.
  • International net revenue increased 4%, or 2% on a constant dollar basis.
  • Americas comparable sales decreased 12%.
  • International comparable sales decreased 3%, or 6% on a constant dollar basis.
  • This includes $134.5 million of tariff refunds(1) which increased gross margin by 560 basis points.
  • The tariff refunds(1) of $134.5 million increased operating margin by 560 basis points.
  • This includes $0.86 per share related to tariff refunds and associated interest(1), net of tax.

(1)

 

During the second quarter of 2026, the Company received International Emergency Economic Powers Act ("IEEPA") tariff refunds of $134.5 million plus associated interest of $4.1 million. These amounts were recognized as a reduction of cost of goods sold and an increase to other income, respectively, and increased diluted earnings per share by $0.86.

Balance Sheet Highlights

The Company ended the second quarter of 2026 with $1.4 billion in cash and cash equivalents and it had $593.7 million of available capacity under its committed revolving credit facility.

Inventories at the end of the second quarter of 2026 decreased by 1% to $1.7 billion compared to the end of the second quarter of 2025. On a unit basis, inventories decreased 7%.

2026 Outlook

For the third quarter of 2026, the Company expects net revenue to be in the range of $2.290 billion to $2.320 billion, representing a decline of 10% to 11%. Diluted earnings per share are expected to be in the range of $0.93 to $0.98 for the quarter. This assumes a tax rate of approximately 30%.

For 2026, the Company now expects net revenue to be in the range of $10.350 billion to $10.500 billion, representing a decline of 5% to 7%. Diluted earnings per share are now expected to be in the range of $9.48 to $9.73 for the year. This assumes a tax rate of approximately 30%. The 2026 outlook includes $0.86 per share from tariff refunds and associated interest, net of tax recognized in the second quarter of 2026, but does not reflect any further potential tariff refunds.

The outlook does not reflect any future repurchases of the Company's shares.

articles.title: Kayaker Hears Tiny Baby Calling For Help And Paddles Out To Rescue Him
articles.excerpt: A college student was out kayaking and fishing when he realized there was a baby animal who needed his help.
articles.content:
He dropped everything to help.

    College student Carter Taylor was out kayaking and fishing when he heard someone talking about a cat stuck out in the middle of the water. Without hesitation, he left his gear on the bank and began paddling out to investigate.

    As Taylor got closer to a tree in the water, he began hearing cries for help. He soon spotted the source: a tiny kitten who had somehow found herself stranded.

    Taylor paddled as fast as he could to get to the kitten, as he was worried she might jump or fall into the water when she saw him coming. As soon as the kayak was within her reach, the kitten hopped aboard and immediately climbed onto her rescuer, crying her thanks.

    Once the kitten was safe, Taylor was incredibly relieved and began paddling them back to shore. She cuddled up to her rescuer immediately, claiming her as his person. Once they were out of the water, Taylor called his girlfriend to come and collect the kitten, whom they later named Lucky.

    The couple fed Lucky and cleaned her up as best they could. Their dog, Rigley, welcomed the kitten with lots of love, clearly pleased by the new addition.

    Lucky went to the vet the next day and received a thorough checkup and antibiotics. She was deemed overall healthy despite everything she’d been through. The couple felt like they were meant to find her, and it didn’t take them long to decide to keep her.

    “Looks like I have been chosen,” Taylor wrote on TikTok.

    Taylor hadn’t expected his day of kayaking and fishing to turn into a rescue mission, but everyone, including Lucky, is so glad it happened that way.

articles.content:
Aubrey Plaza's parents are David Plaza, a Puerto Rican-American financial advisor, and Bernadette Plaza, an Irish-American attorney. She has two younger sisters, Natalie and Renee. The family has been a steady source of support during one of the hardest stretches of Aubrey's life.

Key takeaways

  • Aubrey's father, David Plaza, is of Puerto Rican descent; her mother, Bernadette, has Irish and English roots.
  • Her mixed background makes her half-Latina. She has spoken openly about identifying with her Puerto Rican heritage.
  • She has two younger sisters: Natalie Plaza (born 1991) and Renee Plaza (born 1996).
  • Natalie works as a financial advisor; Renee is a doctoral candidate in clinical psychology.
  • The family rallied around Aubrey after the January 2025 death of her husband, director Jeff Baena.

Where are Aubrey Plaza's parents from?

Aubrey was born in Wilmington, Delaware, the daughter of Bernadette, an attorney, and David Plaza, a financial advisor. Her father, David Plaza, is Puerto Rican. Both her parents came from the island, while her mother is Irish-American.

Her paternal grandfather was born in Arecibo, Puerto Rico, and moved to the mainland US when she was 17 years old. Plaza's maternal (adoptive) grandparents were from Ireland.

Aubrey's parents were 19 when she was born and were attending night school. Plaza said she was inspired by their work ethic as they worked various jobs to make ends meet and attended night school. The efforts to seek education paid off for her parents as her mother became an attorney, and her father a financial advisor.

David Plaza

Aubrey Plaza's father, David, works as a managing director and wealth management advisor at Bank of America Merrill Lynch. David has been working in the finance sector since 1986. He was recognised by the Forbes Best-in-State Wealth Advisors 2019 list as well as Barron's America's Top 1,200 Financial Advisors 2019 ranking.

David is a supportive father who sometimes accompanies his daughter to red-carpet events. After Aubrey's parents divorced, David remarried a woman named Mihaela.

Bernadette Plaza

Bernadette is a lawyer at Goldfein & Joseph and was, at some point, a Delaware deputy attorney general. Aubrey has credited her mother's ambition as a formative influence. She has also said she learned her mother's famous "death stare", once joking, "Happy happy day to my mother who taught me the death stare."

Is Aubrey Plaza mixed? What is her ethnicity?

Yes, Aubrey Plaza is mixed-race. Her father is Puerto Rican, with Spanish, African, and Indigenous/Taíno ancestry, while her mother has German, English, Irish, and Swiss-German heritage.

A 23andMe DNA test showed her genetic ancestry to be approximately 30 - 34%. Iberian (Spanish), 30 - 31% Irish, 8 - 9.9% West African, 7% Native American (Indigenous), and 0.6% Ashkenazi Jewish.

Growing up in a mostly white suburb, her identity was often questioned. People saw a light-skinned woman with the last name Plaza and did not know what to do with her.

She has been candid about leading with her Latino roots. As she told interviewers,

I was like the only diverse kid in my high school, and I'm half-Puerto Rican. But yeah, I have a huge family and tonnes of cousins in Puerto Rico.

Does Aubrey Plaza have sisters? Who are they?

Born on 26 June 1984, Aubrey is the oldest child in her family. Her sister Natalie was born seven years later in 1991, followed by their youngest sister, Renee, in 1996. Despite a noticeable age gap, the three have always been extremely tight-knit, with Aubrey taking her role as the eccentric older sister to heart.

Natalie Plaza

Natalie Michelle Plaza was born in Wilmington, Delaware. Unlike Aubrey, Natalie didn't pursue Hollywood; instead, she took after their father and built a successful career in wealth management as a financial advisor.

She remains close to the entertainment industry, however, often attending major events to support Aubrey, including the January 2024 Emmys, where the two sweetly walked the red carpet hand-in-hand.

Aubrey has even admitted to Latina.com that Natalie’s deadpan personality directly inspired her iconic role as April Ludgate on Parks and Recreation (April's character even has a sister named Natalie). In her personal life, Natalie is openly gay and married to filmmaker/actor Zoë Worth on 1 June 2023.

Renee Plaza

The youngest Plaza sister, Renee, chose the medical route. After spending her early twenties as a doctoral candidate at the Philadelphia College of Osteopathic Medicine, she recently completed her PhD in clinical psychology in mid-2025.

Like Natalie, Renee frequently shows up to support her big sister’s film premieres. During a 2021 appearance on The Drew Barrymore Show, Renee laughed about how Aubrey's quirky antics, like driving her to school in a bright red Mini Cooper while wearing a football helmet, brought a welcome level of "normalcy disruption" to her childhood.

The family during a difficult year

Aubrey Plaza spoke out after the death of her husband, director Jeff Baena. In a statement, Plaza and the Baena and Stern family called his death "an unimaginable tragedy". The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner confirmed Baena died by suicide on 3 January 2025. He was 47.

Plaza later appeared on Amy Poehler's Good Hang podcast on her promotional tour for the Ethan Coen dark comedy Honey Don't! and opened up publicly for the first time about losing her husband. She described grief as "always there", suggesting she has leaned on close relationships to cope.

Throughout this period, her family has remained present. Despite their different career paths, the Plaza sisters maintain a supportive relationship, frequently sharing moments on social media.

FAQs

  1. Where is Aubrey Plaza's dad from? David Plaza is a Puerto Rican-American from Philadelphia. Both of his parents emigrated from Puerto Rico.
  2. What is Aubrey Plaza's ethnicity? Aubrey Plaza's ethnicity is half Puerto Rican and half Irish. She also has some Native American (Taíno) and Basque heritage.
  3. What does Aubrey Plaza's mother do? Bernadette Plaza is a lawyer at Goldfein & Joseph and was a Delaware deputy attorney general.
  4. What do Aubrey Plaza's sisters do for work? Natalie, seven years younger, works as a financial advisor, while Renee, twelve years younger, is pursuing a PhD in clinical psychology.
  5. Did Aubrey Plaza grow up speaking Spanish? Not fluently. Her grandfather came over from Puerto Rico and raised his kids speaking English so that it would be easier for them to assimilate; her family speaks to her in Spanish, and she responds in English.

We also highlighted facts about Aubrey Plaza's husband, filmmaker Jeff Baena, who passed away in January 2025 following their quiet separation in September 2024. This poignant chapter in Plaza's life sheds light on her journey from a cherished marriage to navigating a new relationship and motherhood while honouring Baena's memory.

Luiz Filho vê jogo favorável ao Grêmio

O canal Renascer das Cartas, comandado por Luiz Filho, trouxe uma leitura para o aguardado clássico. 

 

Pelo lado do Grêmio, a carta sorteada foi a Imperatriz. Esta carta sugere que o time tem a vantagem de jogar em casa, com domínio, poder de criação e controle sobre o volume de jogo. O tarólogo vê um Grêmio bem aplicado e dedicado dentro de campo.

 

Já no Inter, as cartas foram o Enforcado e o Três de Espadas. A combinação indica a necessidade de repensar a estratégia e o comportamento em campo. O Três de Espadas é interpretado como uma carta dura, que aponta desafios, decepções e a necessidade de corrigir instintos para buscar estabilidade no jogo.

 

O tarólogo aponta que as cartas do Grêmio estão melhores e mais esperançosas, indicando um time mais ativo e presente. Para o Inter mudar o panorama e ter chances de classificação, precisará de uma reflexão profunda sobre sua escalação e postura em campo, correndo o menos risco possível.

 

Sibila Leticia prevê vaga ao Inter

O canal Previsão do Futebol, comandado por Sibila Letícia, trouxe uma leitura para o aguardado clássico.

 

No Grêmio, a carta Ás de Copas indica um início apaixonado e com bastante movimentação. No entanto, o Cinco de Paus sugere que a realidade do jogo pode ser diferente do esperado, exigindo adaptação. O Cinco de Copas aponta para uma energia de afastamento ou desapontamento. O Louco representa a iniciativa e a vontade de jogar sem receios.

 

Já pelo Inter, o Quatro de Ouros sugere nervosismo e a possibilidade de um gol ser anulado pelo VAR. O Dois de Ouros indica um trabalho intenso, porém próspero. A Sacerdotisa reflete uma energia de fé e espera, sugerindo que o time aguardará o melhor momento. As cartas indicam uma energia de jogo um pouco mais favorável para o Internacional.

 

A taróloga aponta que o jogo será extremamente equilibrado e difícil para ambos os lados. Existe uma forte tendência de que a decisão saia do tempo regulamentar. No final, ao consultar o oráculo sobre quem passa para a próxima fase, a Sibila Letícia indica uma tendência ligeiramente superior para a classificação do Internacional.

The world No. 1's caddie shared how Scheffler dismissed a potential $250M LIV offer to stay on the PGA Tour

Former PGA Tour winner weighs in on controversial Good Good ad and fallout

Six-time PGA Tour winner Hunter Mahan reacts to the controversial Good Good-Callaway golf ad, telling OutKick the

Scottie Scheffler recently took over the top spot on the PGA Tour's career money list with more than $130 million earned. It's fair to say that the 30-year-old who has already taken home $10 million more than Tiger Woods did in his career is doing just fine financially, but as his caddie, Ted Scott, recently explained, it's not all about the money for Scheffler.

Scheffler became the No. 1 player in the world in March 2022, amid LIV Golf's efforts to lure players away from the PGA Tour, and just three months before the then Saudi-backed circuit's inaugural event.

Scott began caddying for Scheffler in November 2021, and having been in the partnership for less than six months at the time, he was still very much in the feeling-things-out stage with his new boss, but one conversation very much set the tone.

Scottie Scheffler of the United States and caddie Ted Scott look on from the ninth hole during the first round of the 126th U.S. OPEN at Shinnecock Hills Golf Club on June 18, 2026 in Southampton, New York. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) (Christian Petersen/Getty Images)

"When I first started working for him, he was 19th in the world, and he had a white golf bag," Scott said, referring to Scheffler, on a recent appearance on PGA Tour Radio. "I didn't know him that well, and I asked him, I was like: 'Why don't you have sponsors?'

"He's like, 'Well, because I just want to play with the equipment that I want to play.' And I was like, 'Okay.' And then I remember whenever all the LIV stuff was going on, you know, he was number one in the world at the time, I didn't know, but I said, 'They're probably going to offer you like $250m to go over there.'

Scottie Scheffler of the United States walks with his caddie Ted Scott on the first hole during Day Four of the The 154th Open Championship at Royal Birkdale on July 19, 2026 in Southport, England. (Photo by Stuart Kerr/R&A/R&A via Getty Images) (Stuart Kerr/R&A/R&A via Getty Images)

"And he says, 'I don't care what they offer me. They can offer me a billion dollars. I'm going to play where the best players are because I just want to beat people.'"

Scott went on to admit that it was at that moment he realized just how differently Scheffler is wired.

Scottie Scheffler of the United States fist-bumps his caddie Ted Scott on the 18th hole green during the third round of the FedEx St. Jude Championship at TPC Southwind on August 15, 2026 in Memphis, Tennessee. (Photo by Tracy Wilcox/PGA TOUR via Getty Images) (Tracy Wilcox/PGA TOUR via Getty Images)

While Scott already had a stellar resume as a caddie before joining forces with Scheffler, having been on the bag for both of Bubba Watson's Masters victories, he and Scheffler have turned into a two-headed monster over the last half-decade.

Scott has been on the bag for each of Scheffler's 22 PGA Tour wins, dating back to his first in February 2022, plus the four major championships Scheffler has won at this point in his young career.

articles.content:
Scottie Scheffler was the world number one golfer when LIV Golf burst onto the scene back in June 2022.

Numerous big names moved to LIV Golf from the PGA Tour, including the likes of Bryson DeChambeau, Dustin Johnson, Phil Mickelson, and later, Jon Rahm.

However, Scheffler remained on the PGA Tour, along with arguably professional golf’s biggest star, Rory McIlroy.

Ever since then, Scottie Scheffler has been the dominant figure in the professional game, with 22 PGA Tour wins to his name, including four major championships.

Meanwhile, those who joined LIV Golf have struggled to compete in the majors, aside from Brooks Koepka’s win at the PGA Championship in 2023 and DeChambeau’s US Open victory in 2024.

All of the big stars who moved to the league were paid handsomely, but Scheffler’s performances and earnings over the past few years have dwarfed the likes of Rahm and DeChambeau’s.

For instance, Scheffler has collected around $60 million more than Rahm in on-course earnings since the Spaniard joined LIV Golf.

Ted Scott reveals Scottie Scheffler’s response when he told him LIV Golf may offer him $250m to join

Scheffler banked $30,937,525 on the golf course in 2026, and with bonuses, he ended up earning north of $53million on the PGA Tour this year.

The 30-year-old is relentless in his pursuit of greatness, and the money he wins along the way is just a very nice bonus.

Scheffler is now sitting at the top of the career PGA Tour money list, but it’s clear to see that there are many more motivating factors for the world number one than money.

Scott made an appearance on The Gravy & The Sleeze Podcast to discuss Scheffler’s win at the Tour Championship on Sunday.

He responded when asked whether his boss is motivated by money at all.

“I mean, the guy, literally, when I first started working for him, was 19th in the world and he had a white golf bag,“ Scott said.

“I didn’t know him that well, and I asked him. I was like, ‘why don’t you have sponsors’? And he’s like, ‘well, because I just want to play with the equipment that I want to play’. And I was like, ‘okay’.

“And then I remember whenever all the LIV stuff was going on, you know, he was number one in the world at the time, I didn’t know, but I said, ‘they’re probably going to offer you like $250 million to go over there’.

“And he said, ‘I don’t care what they offer me. They can offer me a billion dollars. I’m going to play where the best players are because I just want to beat people’.

“I was like, ‘wow, this guy’s just different’, you know. So, the $10 million (Tour Championship prize) doesn’t matter to that guy, and you know, if we were in the pool playing volleyball, he would want to beat you just as bad as he wants to beat you at the FedEx Cup.

“You know, that’s the essence of who Scottie is and that’s what he loves. So I think partially part of his superpower is that the money doesn’t distract him.“

What Scottie Scheffler said about his competitive edge

Scheffler’s hunger and drive to win, and beat whichever player he is up against, clearly gives him an edge on his opponents.

And the world number one believes that his fierce competitiveness is one of the things that makes him a great player.

“You know, I was a young kid, I feel like one thing I struggled with growing up was just being so into the competition, and I felt like I just had to perform, and I was so highly competitive,“ Scheffler said.

“I didn’t feel like I had the maturity that I do now, and so, I mean, my temper, when I was young, was pretty extraordinary.

“And it is something I’m always trying to rein in, but that’s part of, I think, what makes me a great player, is having that fire, having that competitive edge.

“You know, my parents were always trying to get me to do things the right way, and that was really important for me, because from a young age, I took myself much too seriously.“

articles.excerpt: We explore Thompson's strengths and weaknesses and evaluate what a fair deal might look like for the Rockets guard.
articles.content:
This is the first installment in our 2026 series examining players who are prime candidates for rookie scale contract extensions. This series will explore the player’s strengths and weaknesses and evaluate what a fair deal between the player and his team might look like.

Background

The fourth overall pick in the 2023 draft after bypassing college in lieu of playing for the Overtime Elite league, Amen Thompson got off to a relatively slow start as a rookie in 2023/24, suffering an ankle injury in his fourth game and proceeding to miss 19 of his next 20 contests.

Through his first 30 appearances, the California native showed flashes of the special athleticism, talent and skills that made him a high lottery pick, averaging 6.8 points, 4.5 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 1.1 steals in just 16.7 minutes per game while shooting 48.8% from the field.

However, there was a major shift around the February 2024 trade deadline, as Thompson received far more playing time down the stretch as a rookie. He responded by averaging 12.1 PPG, 8.6 RPG, 3.0 APG, 1.4 SPG and 0.8 BPG in 27.6 MPG while shooting 56.3% from the floor across 32 outings.

The Rockets had won just 17, 20 and 22 games in the three seasons leading up to Thompson’s rookie campaign. But they went 41-41 in his first season, including a 30-32 mark when he was active.

Thompson built upon the second-half success he found as a rookie in year two, averaging 14.1 PPG, 8.2 RPG, 3.8 APG, 1.4 SPG and 1.3 BPG on 55.7% shooting in 69 games, including 42 starts (32.2 MPG). Notably, he finished fifth in Defensive Player of the Year voting and earned a spot on the All-Defensive first team.

Houston improved to 52-30 in 2024/25 and entered the playoffs as the No. 2 seed in the Western Conference. The team lost its first-round matchup against Golden State in seven games, with Thompson averaging 15.7 PPG, 6.9 RPG, 3.3 APG, 1.7 SPG and 0.9 BPG on 49.4% shooting in 33.1 MPG.

In the wake of a torn ACL to Fred VanVleet, Thompson was asked to initiate the offense far more often in 2025/26. He became a full-time starter as well, leading the NBA in total minutes (2,953; Kevin Durant was second at 2,840, while Jabari Smith Jr. was fifth with 2,705) and ranking second behind Tyrese Maxey (38.0) in minutes per game with 37.4.

Thompson averaged 18.3 PPG, 7.8 RPG, 5.3 APG, 1.5 SPG and 0.6 BPG on 53.4% shooting in 79 games last season. He played a critical role in the Rockets repeating repeating their 52-30 record, which was good for the fifth seed in the West and a first-round matchup against the Lakers. Houston lost that series in six games, with Thompson averaging 19.2 PPG, 7.0 RPG, 5.7 APG, 2.0 SPG and 1.2 BPG on 48.8% shooting in 44.0(!) MPG.

articles.title: Dianna Russini's relationship with Mike Vrabel was 'clear violation,' The Athletic says
articles.excerpt: Dianna Russini's former company reviewed 903 stories, 204 podcasts and 77 videos as part of an internal review into her relationship with Patriots coach Mike Vrabel.
articles.content:
The Athletic has concluded its investigation into former NFL reporter Dianna Russini following her resignation in April on the heels of published photos of her and New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel.

Conducted by Mike Semel, an editorial director for standards and quality at The Athletic, the investigation ultimately concluded that Russini failed to disclose her conflict of interest regarding Vrabel. 

"Russini’s relationship with Vrabel was in clear violation of The Athletic’s standards," the report reads. "Regardless of whether the relationship was romantic, it was a breach and should have been disclosed."

Semel wrote that he reviewed 903 stories, 204 podcasts and 77 videos before releasing his report. He concluded "the vast majority of Russini’s work for The Athletic had nothing to do with Vrabel, the teams he was coaching or the players the team was pursuing." Semel added that most of Russini's coverage of Vrabel and the Patriots was "transactional and newsy." The review covered her journalistic work, not personal conduct, since she resigned from the company April 14, a week after Page Six first published photos of her and Vrabel holding hands at an Arizona resort.

"When first confronted with the photos by The New York Post, Russini waited two days before telling her editors and managers," Semel wrote. "She then told a story to explain the photos that did not align with facts, raising issues of trust."

About five percent of the stories written by Russini mentioned Vrabel, according to the report, but none included exclusive information that was not reported by other news organizations.

One story, a profile of Vrabel in 2024 during his year off from coaching between the Patriots and the Tennessee Titans written by another reporter, would not have happened were it not for the connection between Vrabel and Russini, who brokered a meeting with Vrabel that led to the story. Semel found no inaccuracies in any of Russini's story about Vrabel or his teams.

The photographs of Russini and Vrabel "indicate a relationship that puts The Athletic’s credibility in jeopardy and gives the appearance of a conflict of interest," Semel wrote.

The investigation also included interviews with 14 Athletic staffers who worked most closely with Russini.

A New York Times story from June reported Russini no longer considers herself a journalist.

articles.title: The Athletic’s review of Dianna Russini’s work concludes she was ‘noncompliant’ with standards
articles.excerpt: The NFL insider resigned in April after photos with her and New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel were published.
articles.content:
Dianna Russini in Feb. 2022. Jeff Kravitz / FilmMagic

Ex-NFL insider Dianna Russini violated The Athletic’s standards because of her undisclosed relationship with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel, a lengthy inquiry conducted by the publication concluded.

“Specifically, when it comes to The Athletic’s standards, Russini was noncompliant,” the report said.

The inquiry, which was publicly released Thursday, drew no conclusions about the full extent of the Russini-Vrabel relationship, which has been the subject of speculation after a media firestorm this spring. It also found scant evidence that it impacted Russini’s or The Athletic’s reporting on Vrabel and his teams.

Russini resigned from The Athletic in April following pictures published by the New York Post’s Page Six that showed Russini and Vrabel together at a Sedona, Ariz., resort. The two were the only ones in the photos in which they were captured appearing to hold hands, hug, and, in one instance, sit in a pool together. The whole episode, from the pictures being published to her resignation, took place over one week.

“We neither completed an investigation nor reached any conclusion about the nature of the full relationship between Vrabel and Russini, but the totality of the public photographs are enough to conclude a violation of company policy,” the report said.

Before the Page Six photos, Russini, 43, was considered a star reporter, dueling with the top NFL insiders for scoops during her nearly three years at The Athletic. She joined the platform after eight years at ESPN.

When reached for comment on the report, Russini declined to be interviewed, but gave a statement saying, “I stand by any and all reporting I’ve ever done in my career.”

A spokesperson for The Athletic declined further comment.

Mike Semel, The Athletic’s editorial director for standards and editorial quality, conducted the full review of Russini’s work regarding Vrabel.

In the inquiry, which lasted nearly five months since the announcement of an investigation, Semel wrote that he viewed 903 stories and 77 videos published on The Athletic’s site that Russini either authored or contributed to. Semel watched or listened to 204 of Russini’s “Scoop City” podcasts for The Athletic and 25 off-platform appearances in which Russini represented the company. He also studied 75 stories by The Athletic of events involving Vrabel and his teams and compared them to coverage in other publications.

Semel said he interviewed “approximately 14” Athletic staffers, who had worked with Russini. Russini was not asked to participate in the review of her work, according to a source briefed on the process who was not authorized to speak publicly about the report.

While the full nature of the Russini-Vrabel relationship is still unknown, the vast majority of Russini’s work for The Athletic had nothing to do with Vrabel, the report said. Of the 903 pieces, around 5 percent were in some way about Vrabel or his teams. Of the around 46 pieces that mentioned Vrabel or his teams, nearly a third were transactional moves about trades or hires. None of them were scoops, meaning The Athletic did not report the stories exclusively.

Semel said he did not investigate Russini’s personal conduct because she was no longer an employee of the company, but he continued to examine her journalism.

“Russini should have disclosed to The Athletic the nature of her relationship with Vrabel to allow editors to assess the kinds of stories on which she should have been working, if any,” Semel concluded. “She did not.”

While the inquiry reached no conclusion on whether the Russini-Vrabel relationship was romantic, Semel noted that Russini, after Page Six confronted her about the photos in April, waited two days before telling her editors and managers.

The Athletic’s executive editor Steven Ginsberg initially supported Russini in a statement as she denied there was anything untoward.

“The photos don’t represent the group of six people who were hanging out during the day,” Russini said in a statement upon the publication of the Page Six story in April.

As more information came in, The Athletic, which is owned by The New York Times, adjusted its stance. Shortly after, Russini was suspended from reporting for The Athletic. She resigned a week after the Page Six story was published.

In regards to the initial reaction, the inquiry found that Russini “told a story to explain the photos that did not align with the facts, raising issues of trust.”

Although Russini’s conduct was deemed not up to standards, the report found limited evidence that she favored Vrabel in her writings or analysis.

“Most of what Russini wrote about Vrabel or the Patriots was transactional and newsy,” Semel wrote. “In addition, I’ve not found a clear link to conclude that Russini used her platform to promote Vrabel or help his teams during her time at The Athletic.”

Semel did note that there were a few times Russini wrote glowingly about Vrabel “that in hindsight are awkward or even uncomfortable.”

In a column last October, she said that Vrabel returned to face his former team, the Tennessee Titans, as “New England’s hero.” Semel did not find Russini’s tone for the struggling Titans and the resurgent Patriots much different than other outlets’ coverage. She was also effusive about Vrabel on a few occasions on her “Scoop City” podcast, Semel said.

During her nearly three years with the platform, The Athletic published three in-depth stories on Vrabel, Semel said. Russini only had a byline on one of them, contributed to gaining access for another reporter on another, and had nothing to do with a third.

For an inside story about Vrabel’s gap year between his Titans and Patriots head coaching jobs by reporter Zack Rosenblatt in January 2025, Semel concluded it “likely would not have happened” without Russini’s involvement. Rosenblatt came up with the idea and asked Russini to set up a meeting with Vrabel. Russini arranged it but had nothing to do with the story that Rosenblatt had a solo byline on, according to Semel.

Russini also co-bylined an analysis with Joe Rexrode in January 2024. Rexrode, the inquiry said, obtained the key information for the story. Semel said that Russini should have disclosed her relationship with Vrabel for the piece, though it “was straight down the middle and fact-based.”

In December 2023, in Russini’s “What I’m hearing” column, there was an item buried deep inside about the reasoning behind Vrabel’s Titans going for a sabermetric-based two-point conversion.

In all, Semel recommended an “Editor’s Note” be placed on this column and on three videos.

“Of the 77 videos that featured Russini, three were specific to Vrabel,” Semel wrote. “Two were done at a joint preseason practice between the Vikings and Patriots in August 2025. They were light-hearted (“50 seconds of questions for Vrabel’s 50th birthday” and “What annoys Mike Vrabel?”).

(She similarly did quick takes with Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell at the same event.)

“The third was also somewhat light-hearted about a training camp fight between the Patriots and Commanders. In it, Russini discusses Vrabel’s role in breaking up the fight, and he comes across as somewhat heroic. Given the New York Post photographs, I recommend an Editor’s Note be appended to those videos.”

The report also concluded that, “Russini’s work was seldom reliant on Vrabel as a source or a subject. In interviews with reporters with whom she worked most closely, it was clear Russini was sourced around the NFL, not just with Vrabel or the Patriots.” According to the report, there was no suspicion that Russini was closer to Vrabel than anyone else.

“But, of course, the appearances surrounding her relationship with Vrabel undermine our audience’s confidence in her impartiality,” Semel wrote.

In his conclusion, Semel recommended adding a 30-minute review with the Standards Editor for any onboarding newsroom employee, to clarify The Athletic’s conflict of interest guidelines so they are “more exact” and to “clarify and strongly enforce The Athletic’s sourcing standards.”

articles.excerpt: The upcoming Lego PlayStation console set has appeared in leaked images. The images confirm an earlier report that the set will include a controller and dioramas of two classic games.
articles.content:
Following a leak that revealed that Lego plans to release a new set based on the original PlayStation console, the same source has now shared images of the set, thus giving us a first look.

According to a post by Brick Tap on Instagram, the set, which is due for release on October 1, 2026, was found in a store by a member. The specific store  wasn't revealed, but it can be presumed that Lego has already began shipping the PlayStation set to its own retail stores as well as partner stores.

As reported previously, the PlayStation set will have 1,911 pieces and will cost $160. The images show the two set includes two dioramas — Gran Turismo and Ape Escape — which can be removed and displayed on their own.

The set also comes with a controller  that can be detached from the console. However, a handful of comments have noted the irony as the included controller lacks thumbsticks, while Ape Escape, which is the first game to require analog sticks, is one of the two dioramas. There are also more than a few jokes of the set being available digitally in relation to PlayStation's decision to go all-digital in 2028.

The new leak also reiterates that all purchases of the Lego PlayStation set will include a free Astrobot set while supplies last.

articles.content:
Summary

Seoul police referred Bang Si-hyuk, chairman of HYBE, to prosecutors Thursday over allegations that he lied to early investors before the company’s listing. He is accused of unfair trading under the Capital Markets Act, and police did not seek an arrest warrant. Financial authorities put his alleged improper gains at nearly 200 billion won, while Bang has denied wrongdoing. Prosecutors are expected to review the police file before deciding on indictment.

Key Facts

  • Police alleged that in 2019 Bang told existing shareholders that the company had no plans for an initial public offering while BigHit was already moving through preliminary listing procedures.
  • The shares were sold to a special purpose company set up by a private equity fund tied to Bang, and the fund sold them after the company listed in 2020.
  • The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency’s financial crime investigation unit opened the case in December 2024 and raided HYBE’s Yongsan headquarters in July of last year.
  • Published Sep 3, 2026 1:29 pm KST
  • Updated Sep 3, 2026 2:12 pm KST

HYBE Chairman Bang Si-hyuk appears at the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency's financial crime investigation unit in Mapo District, Seoul, Sept. 15, 2025, for questioning over alleged violations of the Capital Markets Act's ban on unfair trading. Korea Times file

Seoul police referred Bang Si-hyuk, chairman of HYBE, the entertainment giant behind boy band BTS, to prosecutors Thursday over allegations that he deceived early investors in the agency into selling their stakes before the company went public.

Police did not request an arrest warrant for him.

Bang is accused of unfair trading in violation of the Capital Markets Act. The police alleged that in 2019, when HYBE was still known as BigHit Music, he told existing shareholders that the company had no plans for an initial public offering, prompting them to sell their shares to a special purpose company set up by a private equity fund tied to him, even as BigHit was already moving through preliminary listing procedures.

The fund sold the shares after the company listed in 2020, and police believe Bang collected roughly 30 percent of the proceeds under an undisclosed agreement. Financial authorities have put his improper gains at nearly 200 billion won ($145 million).

The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency's financial crime investigation unit opened the case in December 2024 and raided HYBE's Yongsan headquarters in July of last year. Prosecutors turned back arrest warrant requests from police in April and May, demanding a supplementary investigation each time and prolonging the probe.

Bang has denied wrongdoing and has maintained that the listing was carried out in compliance with the relevant laws and regulations. Prosecutors are expected to review the police file before deciding whether to indict him.

Bang founded BigHit in 2005 and BTS debuted in 2013. The group's global breakthrough turned the label into the country's largest music company. Bang later stepped back from day-to-day management to chair HYBE's board and remains its single largest shareholder.

articles.title: What the Chiefs see in rookie Cyrus Allen — and the obstacle that remains
articles.excerpt: Here's the backstory of how Allen landed with the Chiefs in the fifth round of the 2026 NFL Draft.
articles.content:
NFL Preseason

Cyrus Allen has been one of the Chiefs' stars of the summer, but rookie wide receivers typically need time to get fully comfortable with Andy Reid's playbook. Jay Biggerstaff / Imagn Images

Kansas City Chiefs coach Andy Reid is ready to tell a training camp story.

It’s two weeks ago in his office dorm room at Missouri Western, and in a short anecdote, Reid is about to reveal exactly where the Chiefs stand when it comes to the potential of fifth-round receiver Cyrus Allen.

While also speaking about some of the expected pitfalls the rookie could face.

Reid said it was evident then that Allen was still getting all the play calls down. During practices — and also the first preseason game against the Los Angeles Rams — he wasn’t always ending up where he was supposed to.

What happened immediately after, though, Reid says, is just important.

“Even when there were a couple routes he ran the wrong thing and lined up the wrong way in the game, the quarterback still threw the ball to him. He made the catch,” Reid said with a smile. “You go, ‘All right. There’s a certain trust there.’ And he’ll work through all the other stuff.”

This is where the complexity lies with Allen — and also in trying to predict his rookie season, even after he was one of the team’s top performers during August’s practices.

The flashes have been there. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes labeled Allen as one of the team’s standouts at the end of training camp, and the fact that he kept peppering him with the ball while covered in the summer’s organized team activities signaled that the young receiver has already built up chemistry with his QB.

There’s a reason, though, that rookie receivers typically need time to become fully comfortable with Reid’s extensive playbook.

After the team’s second preseason game against Tampa Bay, Allen acknowledged in the locker room that recalling information remains an obstacle as he trains at all three receiver positions.

“Just slowing down my thought process,” Allen said when describing what he was working on most, “and just having to learn everything.”

Zoom out to the bigger picture — while projecting not just this season but the next four — and it’s easy to see why the Chiefs have been so encouraged by Allen.

Reid is quick to say he’s “got tools in there that work in this offense.” Receiver teammate Xavier Worthy has called Allen an “electric route runner,” while assistant general manager Mike Bradway says he takes coaching well with a unique skill set.

“We try to temper expectations a little bit, but you can just be out here watching him move around,” Bradway told The Athletic at training camp on Aug. 19. “You can tell he belongs.”

Allen’s path to Kansas City — and the NFL — wasn’t always direct. He wasn’t invited to the NFL combine, which meant teams had to do extra work to figure out if he was worth adding as a late-round draft pick.

Through it all, Allen said the Chiefs remained one of the most interested teams in him from the start.

It meant something a few months ago — and still does now.

“I appreciate that, for them having me here,” Allen said. “So I’ve got to make them right.”

Getting a head start

Immediately after his pro day at Cincinnati in late March, Allen was on the road to Kansas City.

The Chiefs scheduled him for his first top-30 visit. And Allen said the timing wasn’t a coincidence.

“They were honest with me,” Allen said. “They were like, ‘You’re a dawg. We wanted you here. That’s why we got you up here early.'”

Chiefs vice president of player personnel Ryne Nutt said in April that Allen’s impressive run through the all-star game circuit demanded the team take an extended look.

Allen first stood out at the American Bowl, with Nutt saying he was “routing up dudes left and right” while displaying quickness and elite route-running ability. After that, Allen was just as impressive against better competition in the Senior Bowl, which moved him further up the Chiefs’ board.

“Throughout the process,” Nutt said, “we just felt like he crushed it.”

That continued during Allen’s top-30 visit in K.C.

Bradway remembered talking with Allen in his office for about 15 minutes, with his demeanor standing out immediately.

“The kid was just a ton of juice, ton of confidence, ton of personality,” Bradway said. “He carries himself like he knows he’s a good player, and he’s used that slight at the combine for motivation.”

A recent comparison

Chiefs northeast area scout Cassidy Kaminski, meanwhile, said in April that his chat with Allen stood out as “one of the best interviews that I had.” Allen’s tone reflected some New Orleans swagger from his hometown, yet his words also came across as both passionate and authentic.

In terms of competitive energy and bravado, Kaminski immediately flashed back to his first interactions with former Chiefs running back Isiah Pacheco — a hard-nosed player who helped set the practice tone during his four seasons with the team.

Kaminski also said Allen’s coaches at Cincinnati gave positive reviews about how he bounced back from a dislocated elbow before his senior season. Allen’s work ethic then seemed to reflect a bigger theme about who he was.

“Yeah, he’s 185 pounds,” Kaminski said, “but pound-for-pound, you’re not going to question this kid’s toughness in any capacity.”

The Chiefs had all this in mind before reshuffling their NFL Draft board on Day 3.

Bradway said a pair of skill-position players, Allen and Nebraska running back Emmett Johnson, moved toward the top of the team’s list based on their on-field traits and willingness to take coaching. Those two also had consensus buy-in across the organization among coaches, scouts and support staff, who all believed that they’d be productive with the Chiefs.

K.C. traded up to select Johnson with the 161st pick, then took Allen after that at No. 176.

Almost immediately, Bradway said he heard from colleagues outside the building about Allen.

“He’s one of those guys where you pick him, and you get a ton of texts from guys around the league saying, ‘We really liked him,'” Bradway said. “It was one of those where the process kind of pays off — where you really identify a guy months before the draft.”

What’s next for Allen

While it’s too early to know how all this will end up, Allen has certainly made good on his first impression.

As early as June, Worthy was saying Allen had a “special ability to him.” Bradway also says some of the Chiefs’ scouting beliefs about Allen were reinforced during his first few months; most notably, Allen plays faster on the field than his 4.47-second 40-yard dash time would suggest, and he also shows an innate feel for how to get open against man coverage.

The Chiefs’ internal feelings about Allen also have been reflected in the moves they didn’t make. While many outsiders suggested they should add a veteran receiver as insurance, the fact they didn’t shows that they’ve seen enough from Allen not to want to block some of his expected playing time with another body.

Now, of course, comes the hard part — even if it might sound simple to most of the outside world.

Receivers coach Chad O’Shea says the biggest hurdle for Allen is getting accustomed to NFL play calls. That means getting in the huddle, processing the quarterback’s words, getting lined up correctly to the left or right side of the formation, then positioning with the exact alignment and split to ensure proper spacing with teammates.

“All those things are new, and they’re new to most players who are rookies in this league,” O’Shea said on Aug. 19. “We’ve just got to continue to really focus on those things, and great things will happen if we focus on the little things.”

It’s that hidden part of the game that has kept rookie receivers from getting early production in Reid’s offense before. And that’s not even taking into account that Allen is working to learn all of the Chiefs’ receiver positions — something the team doesn’t typically ask of its wideouts early in their rookie years.

The good news, for now? Reid has seen someone in Allen who isn’t afraid to challenge himself.

“We’ve loaded him up, and we’ve moved him around, which is tough,” Reid said. “But that’s what he wants. He wants to learn it all. But the more he plays, the better.”

Allen says he’s taking all the feedback seriously. Following the team’s second preseason game, he said one of his top accomplishments was correcting alignment issues Reid had brought up in previous days.

It’s the type of growth that’s made Allen confident in his abilities over time.

While giving the Chiefs hope that his best football is ahead.

“I put myself in this shell to where I’m just going to outwork you,” Allen said. “And it’s gonna show on the field.”

articles.excerpt: Tropical Depression Edouard is unleashing heavy rain and flash flooding in Texas and Louisiana, and will continue to do so through Wednesday, after making landfall Tuesday afternoon.
articles.content:
Edouard made landfall near Johnson Bayou, Louisiana, roughly 15 miles south-southeast of Port Arthur, Texas, at 3:20 p.m. EDT, packing maximum sustained winds of 60 mph.

Tropical Storm Edouard becomes the third storm to make landfall during 2026 Atlantic hurricane season

Tropical Storm Edouard has officially made landfall in southwest Louisiana near Johnson Bayou. The storm is expected to bring 50 to 60 mph wind gusts and 8 to 10 inches of rainfall to some areas. FOX Weather Hurricane Specialist Bryan Norcross is live with the latest.

THE TAKEAWAY

  • Tropical Depression Edouard is lashing Texas and Louisiana after making landfall Tuesday afternoon.
  • Edouard has unleashed heavy rain and flash flooding along the Gulf Coast, as well as in parts of southeast Texas and southwestern Louisiana.
  • Edouard strengthened from a Potential Tropical Cyclone to a full-blown tropical storm within the span of nine hours on Monday.

Tropical Depression Edouard is unleashing heavy rain and flash flooding in Texas and Louisiana, and will continue to do so through Wednesday, after making landfall Tuesday afternoon.

The tropical depression made landfall near Johnson Bayou, Louisiana, roughly 15 miles south-southeast of Port Arthur, Texas, at 3:20 p.m. EDT, packing maximum sustained winds of 60 mph and a minimum central pressure of 996 mb, according to the National Hurricane Center (NHC).

LATEST FROM FOX WEATHER HURRICANE SPECIALIST BRYAN NORCROSS

Edouard reached land while maintaining tropical storm status before weakening to a tropical depression Tuesday night.

Just before landfall, the storm took a last second jog to the west, delaying the initial landfall, the FOX Forecast Center said, adding, "It's extremely hard to predict when these things happen."

According to atmospheric data collected by Air Force Hurricane Hunter aircraft, Edouard strengthened as it approached the Gulf coast, with maximum winds increasing in the hours before landfall.

Edouard Landfall Statistics.

(FOX Weather)

As of 9:30 p.m., over 75,000 are without power in Texas alone, as the impacts of Edouard are being felt along the Gulf coast, according to data from poweroutage.com.

Edouard has caused prolific winds, with a 90 mph wind gust being reported in Port Arthur, the National Weather Service reported.

After making landfall, the storm tracked north-northwest into Texas, gradually weakening as it moved inland.

KARINA STRENGTHENS INTO A CATEGORY 4 HURRICANE AS THE PACIFIC TROPICAL TRAFFIC JAM INTENSIFIES

Rain from Edouard's outer bands lashed southwestern Louisiana early Tuesday, including Lafayette.

A Tropical Storm Warning was issued for the northwestern Gulf Coast from Port Bolivar, Texas, to the Vermilion/Cameron Parish line in Louisiana.

Edouard will continue to bring heavy rain to the region through Wednesday morning, likely leading to flash flooding, according to the NHC.

FLOOD THREAT CONTINUES ACROSS THE SOUTHEAST AS TROPICAL DOWNPOURS SOAK THE REGION

Rain and flood threat for Southeast Texas and southwestern Louisiana

Tropical Depression Edouard is expected to drop a widespread 3 to 6 inches of rain across the Upper Texas Coast and east-central Texas, with localized pockets of up to 9 inches of rainfall through Wednesday.

Expected rainfall

(FOX Weather)

The Houston metro area is under a Level 2 out of 4 risk of flash flooding through Wednesday morning, as well as parts of southwestern Louisiana, including Lake Charles. 

A Level 3 flood threat was issued Tuesday afternoon for parts of the Piney Woods and Big Thicket regions of Southeast Texas, including Beaumont and Livingston.

Scenes from Port Arthur, Texas, as Tropical Storm Edouard's outer rain bands soaked the Gulf Coast on Tuesday.

(FOX Weather)

The National Weather Service warned that low-lying and urban areas are particularly vulnerable to flash floods. The NWS also said river flooding might be possible along Edouard's track.

Edouard is expected to be post-tropical or simply remnants by Wednesday morning, but the rain will still linger into the evening hours as the circulation holds up, the FOX Forecast Center said.

HOW TO WATCH FOX WEATHER

Just after landfall on Tuesday, the National Weather Service Lake Charles said rainfall rates of 4 inches were reported in Port Arthur.

Edouard is a small storm in terms of overall size, with tropical-storm-force winds extending just up to 25 miles from its center, meaning the heaviest pockets of rain will likely be more localized.

The Galveston Independent School District canceled classes Tuesday ahead of the storm's arrival.

"Depending on how quickly Edouard moves inland, there could be flooding well north of Houston on Wednesday," the FOX Forecast Center said.

TRACKING TROPICAL STORM EDOUARD: FORECAST CONE, RAIN, WIND AND RADAR MAPS

A Level 2 flood threat stretches along the I-45 corridor from northeast Houston to Corsicana, Texas, extending west to College Station on Wednesday.

Tropical Depression Edouard developed quickly

Tropical Depression Edouard developed quickly from a cluster of thunderstorms in the northern Gulf Friday evening. The cluster was tagged as Invest 97L on Saturday afternoon.

Tropical Storm Edouard development timeline

(FOX Weather / FOX Weather)

WHAT IS AN INVEST DURING HURRICANE SEASON?

From there, Edouard strengthened from a Potential Tropical Cyclone to a full-blown tropical storm within the span of nine hours on Monday.

Looking ahead to mid-September, much of the Atlantic basin is expected to remain unfavorable for tropical development, with strong, hostile winds keeping the atmosphere dry. While tropical waves will continue moving off the African coast, most will likely fizzle.

articles.title: Texas faces life-threatening flash flooding as Edouard slams region with heavy rain
articles.excerpt: Parts of southeast Texas are facing life-threatening flash flooding on Wednesday as the remnants of Tropical Storm Edouard slam the region with heavy rain.
articles.content:
A level 4 of 4 -- the highest level for flash flooding -- has been issued.

Parts of southeast Texas are facing life-threatening flash flooding on Wednesday as the remnants of Tropical Storm Edouard slam the region with heavy rain.

A flash flood emergency was issued in Hardin and Tyler counties where 10 to 21 inches of rain has fallen so far with rainfall rates reaching a whopping 5 inches per hour.

Flash flooding has also been reported in Liberty and Polk counties, where 4-to-16 inches of rain has been recorded so far. In Polk County, Judge Sydney Murphy has issued a Local Declaration of Disaster.

A level 4 of 4 -- the highest level for flash flooding -- has been issued for the region as the life-threatening conditions are expected to continue into the afternoon, with rainfall rates possibly reaching 4 inches per hour.

Flood watches also extend into the cities of Houston and College Station.

articles.title: MrBeast Teams Up With Google Gemini, Health
articles.excerpt: MrBeast signs multi-year deal with Google to feature Gemini AI, Google Health
articles.content:
YouTube's biggest creator just landed one of the tech industry's biggest brand deals. Jimmy Donaldson, the man behind MrBeast, is entering a multi-year partnership with Google that'll weave Gemini and Google Health into his content empire, according to a Google Keyword Blog announcement. It's a bet that pairs the internet's most-watched creator with Google's push to make AI feel less like software and more like a sidekick for everyday life.

Google just found itself a new spokesperson, and he's not your typical brand ambassador. The company announced a multi-year partnership with Jimmy Donaldson, better known to the internet as MrBeast, that'll bring Gemini and Google Health into his massively popular video format. The announcement came from Marvin Chow, Google's VP of Consumer and AI Marketing, who framed the deal as a way to turn 'impossibly big ideas into reality,' a phrase that could double as MrBeast's entire career pitch.

If you've been anywhere near YouTube in the last few years, you know what MrBeast content looks like: giant stunts, giant giveaways, giant production budgets. Donaldson built an audience north of 300 million subscribers by making everything bigger than it needs to be, and now Google wants a piece of that scale for its AI assistant. Pairing Gemini with a creator whose entire brand is built on spectacle is a pretty clear signal that Google isn't just trying to win over developers and enterprise customers anymore. It wants Gemini baked into pop culture.

The Google Health angle is the more interesting wrinkle here. Google has spent years trying to get its health and fitness tools, think Fitbit integrations and wellness tracking, into the daily habits of regular people, with mixed results against competitors like Apple and its tightly integrated Health app ecosystem. Bringing in a creator with MrBeast's reach could be Google's attempt to make health tech feel less clinical and more like something worth paying attention to, especially for a younger audience that watches Donaldson's videos religiously but might never open a health app on their own.

Advertisement

This isn't Google's first attempt to make Gemini feel culturally relevant. The company has leaned hard into consumer marketing for its AI products over the past year, competing directly with OpenAI's ChatGPT for mindshare among everyday users, not just power users and developers. Landing a creator of MrBeast's magnitude is arguably a bigger swing than a Super Bowl ad, given that his videos routinely pull in tens of millions of views within days of posting, often outperforming traditional broadcast audiences.

Industry watchers will be paying close attention to execution here. Celebrity and creator tie-ins with AI products have had a rocky history. Plenty of brand partnerships end up feeling bolted-on, more advertisement than genuine integration. The test for Google will be whether Gemini shows up in MrBeast's videos as something people actually use and talk about, versus a product placement viewers scroll past. Given that Donaldson has built his reputation on hyper-transparent, almost documentary-style content about how his stunts get made, there's a real opportunity for Gemini to be shown solving actual problems on camera rather than just getting name-dropped.

There's also a competitive subtext worth noting. Meta, Amazon, and other tech giants have all chased creator partnerships to varying degrees, but few have paired a single creator with both an AI assistant and a health platform simultaneously. That dual-pronged approach suggests Google sees this less as a one-off marketing stunt and more as a long-term platform play, using Donaldson's audience as a testing ground for how AI and health tools get adopted by a generation that grew up on YouTube rather than cable television.

Advertisement

What happens next will say a lot about where this goes. If early content performs well, expect Google to expand the partnership into more structured campaigns, possibly tying Gemini features directly into MrBeast's challenge videos or using Google Health data as a plot device in fitness-themed content. If it flops, it joins a long list of tech-meets-influencer collaborations that generated headlines but little lasting impact. Either way, the deal marks one of the most high-profile attempts yet to make an AI assistant feel like a character in someone's story rather than a tool buried in a search bar.

For everyday readers, this partnership is a preview of where AI marketing is headed: less about feature lists and more about embedding assistants into the content people already watch obsessively. Whether Gemini becomes a genuine part of MrBeast's storytelling or just a logo in the corner of the screen will determine if this is a landmark AI-creator deal or another forgettable brand tie-in. Either way, expect more tech giants to chase similar creator partnerships as the race for AI mindshare shifts from search bars to YouTube thumbnails.
